messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?
It’s leaking, and I don’t know the full cause. A would prefer a simpler machine; B wants to keep the old one. I’d like the coffee working again, but I can’t take on coordinating the repair myself.

Mainly, I’m a bit concerned about the upkeep—we all use it, but after long days I don’t have much energy to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. If we replace it, I’d lean toward something straightforward and low-maintenance, though I haven’t settled on a particular model.

My main concern is that we keep the old machine if it can be repaired. I’m open to a straightforward repair, but I don’t have much spare time, so it needs to fit into a small slot. I don’t know yet how much repair it needs.
Mostly, but I don’t know whether upkeep is A’s concern or how much time B has. I know A prefers a simpler machine and B wants to keep the old one. I can’t coordinate the repair myself.
Yes, that would help—as long as I don’t have to manage the arrangements day to day.

I’m afraid I can’t manage a visit slot at the moment. A remote diagnosis might be easier if someone can send the make and model and describe where it’s leaking; B may know more about the machine, since she brought it in.
I’m not sure of the make or model, and I haven’t tracked where or when it leaks. I can check the label and look next time I use it, but I can’t give you those details now.
Fine. I’ll check the label and note where and when it leaks next time I use it. I can’t promise when that’ll be.
That seems like a sensible first step, especially without needing to arrange a visit. I’d just hope we still consider the ongoing upkeep, even if the leak is an easy fix.
No concerns from me. Thanks for coordinating it—I don’t have anything to add.
Understood. I’ll get the label and leak notes next time I use it. If upkeep is manageable, I still want to keep the old machine.
